top_violation_types.title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: A child did not have their hands washed following a diaper change.

top_violation_types.title: Children Handwashing After Outdoor Activities (26 TAC §746.3417(4))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: After outdoor activities, children did not have their hands washed. Additionally, the children immediately transitioned to lunch time and did not wash their hands prior to eating.

top_violation_types.title: Required Admission Information-Child's allergies and Completed Food Allergy Plan (26 TAC §746.605(15))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The standard is evaluated for a standard investigation and is not compliant. The operation does not have a complete food allergy plan for a child with a diagnosis food allergy.

top_violation_types.title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(1)(A))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The director's files is incomplete and does not have proof of orientation, DL/ID, pre-affidavit, nor an signed affidavit.

top_violation_types.title: Prohibited Punishments - Restrictive device for time out (26 TAC §746.2805(8))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: A 18 mo old was observed to be sitting in a highchair upon arrival. A volunteer was observed removing the child from the chair and telling them they could not hit and not to hit again. The caregiver of the gorup initally stated the chair is only used for eating. After being informed of the volunteer's statement, the caregiver then stated it is used but for only 1 minute.

top_violation_types.title: Infant Handwashing - Raised to Sink (26 TAC §746.3421(b))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The sink in the infant room was not operational. The infants were not having their hands washed with soap and water.  This was corrected at the inspection when the infants were moved to a classroom with a proper working sink.

top_violation_types.title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: During the investigation and video, it was found that the caregiver did not demonstrate a high level of judgment or self-control.

top_violation_types.title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §746.201(1))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operational policies were not complete.
